summary: The audit confirms an elevated risk profile driven by a combination of manifest‐level weaknesses—multiple unprotected exported components, debug mode, and permissive backup settings—paired with code that contains several high‑impact vulnerabilities such as SQL injection, command injection, insecure WebView usage, cleartext network traffic, and unencrypted file writes. The overlap between the two views highlights a high likelihood of data exposure and exploitation of internal business logic via external app interaction.
top_risks: Unprotected exported components enable external intent injection and potential misuse of internal logic
Runtime.exec called with unsanitized data allows arbitrary command execution
Dynamic execSQL/rawQuery usage permits SQL injection attacks
Hardcoded HTTP endpoints and debuggable build expose traffic to sniffing
Unencrypted file writes combined with allowBackup increase data leakage risk
correlations: Unprotected exported service/receiver can trigger malicious intents that reach insecure SQL or runtime exec code
Backup data can include unencrypted files written by the app
Debuggable configuration aids analysis of cleartext traffic and vulnerable code paths
Public content provider coupled with raw SQL may expose sensitive tables
Untrusted WebView URL may be used by external components to deliver malicious content
recommended_next_steps: Mark all exported components as non‑exported or guard them with permission checks and intent validations
Replace execSQL/rawQuery with parameterized prepared statements and audit all SQL dynamic content
Sanitize all input to Runtime.exec, restrict commands to a whitelist or remove usage
Eliminate hardcoded HTTP; enforce HTTPS via Network Security Config and certificate pinning
Encrypt all sensitive data and store it in internal, app‑private storage; disable allowBackup or enable backup encryption; remove android:debuggable from release builds
